title: Apollo 11 AS-506 event and parking-orbit benchmark

source.citation: NASA CR-61291, AS-506 "G" Manned Lunar Landing Mission Post-Launch Operational Trajectory for July 16, 1969, Northrop Corporation, August 1969
source.report_statement: The report contains the real-time operational trajectory using the actual Greenwich Mean Time Guidance Reference Release supplied by the Manned Spacecraft Center.

extraction.method: Read the report's embedded text for Tables 2.1 and 2.4; visually verify the retained summary values against rendered PDF pages 122-123. Manually transcribe the Table 2.2 launch state from rendered PDF page 18, EPOI state/geodetic coordinates from pages 50 and 54, four intermediate geodetic checkpoints, and staged vehicle mass rows from pages 13, 25, 26 and 49. Check launch/EPOI vector norms against scalar summary values. The SSATK demo derives a proper fixed-frame rotation by aligning the launch state with the WGS84/IERS-B pad state, then checks the result against the Table 2.2 EPOI and intermediate geodetic coordinates. NASA-TM-X-62812 provides a separate approximate AS-506 mass history and total propellant-consumption summary. This inferred orientation and operational guidance product are source-closure evidence, not independent frame or flight truth. No OCR-derived trajectory profile is included in the package.
limitations: The operational guidance trajectory is not raw sensor telemetry or an independent post-flight best-estimate trajectory.
NASA CR-61291 Tables 2.1 and 2.4 report different S-II center-engine-cutoff times; the discrepancy remains unresolved.
NASA CR-61291 Table 2.4 and the Apollo 11 Mission Report differ in maximum dynamic pressure (34725.243 Pa versus 735 lb/ft^2, or 35191.990351 Pa); retain both source values.
Table 2.2 reports total vehicle mass increasing by 919.32 kg from S-II cutoff to S-IVB ullage ignition; this interval is preserved but not used as a mass-conservation reference.
The Table 2.2 insertion state and Table 2.4 eccentricity/period do not close as one osculating two-body orbit under SSATK's Earth gravitational parameter.
Table 2.4's printed twice-specific-energy sign conflicts with its bound-orbit eccentricity and period; specific energy is excluded.
The event summary supports benchmark closure only; it does not provide the full trajectory samples or engineering inputs for predictive ascent simulation.
A benchmark pass against this report does not establish flight qualification or independent measured-flight accuracy.
